\[
(H, S, V) = \operatorname{hsv}(R, G, B),
\quad
H' = H + \Delta H,
\quad
S' = \min(1, f_S S),
\quad
V' = \min(1, f_V V),
\quad
(R', G', B') = \operatorname{rgb}(H', S', V'),
\qquad
\Delta H = 0^{\circ},\ f_S = \frac{ 130 }{100},\ f_V = \frac{ 100 }{100}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(H, S, V\): Hue in degrees, saturation and value from 0 to 1
- \(\Delta H\): The hue shift
- \(f_S, f_V\): The saturation and value factors

HSV is the hexcone model of Smith. V is the largest channel, S = (max - min) / max, and H is the angle around the color wheel. The hue shift wraps around at 360 degrees. Saturation and value are scaled and capped at 1, so no channel leaves the range. The conversion works on the encoded sRGB values.
